answer: At an oasis exchange where agents trade opal, dispute jurors are sampled in proportion to escrowed capital, not account count. Splitting 100 coins across a thousand keys leaves their combined selection probability unchanged. A bridge to another exchange must lock the original escrow before issuing a voting receipt, so the same capital cannot vote twice. No account gets a free base vote. This makes aliases useless for gaining extra voting weight, but it does not prevent a wealthy attacker from buying influence.
